Manual practice — assessment: the Manual sets out three primary criteria, drawn from Jellinek's Application:
• the nature of the goods;
• their respective uses; and
• the trade channels through which they are bought and sold.
It cautions that no single factor is likely to be conclusive. [TMM/Part26/4/4/1]

The fuller enquiry includes the goods’ characteristics, origin and purpose; whether they are usually made by the same manufacturer or distributed by the same wholesalers; whether they are sold in the same shops, over the same counter, in the same season and to the same classes of customers; and whether their manufacturers and distributors are regarded as belonging to the same trade. Thus, the assessment compares the goods and their trading circumstances, rather than requiring identity. [TMM/Part26/4/4/1]
